is the second chapter in the (hopefully) ongoing Deus Ex "reboot" series. It improves a lot upon the predecessor
and is an all-round impressive game, which brings many new ways to play and more creative ways to progress through missions. Also, that thing with the microtransactions and P2W stuff really doesn't affect gameplay and you can easily progress without it.
-GAMEPLAY & STORY:
Like its predecessor, the gameplay consists mainly of sneaking about in 1st person and quietly taking down enemies, hacking cameras and occasionally, shooting some guys. However there is more freedom in ways to play than in HR.
More weapons and augments allow for a more FPS-esque gameplay, rather than stealthing about.
The story continues, where HR left off and smoothly skips over the endings of HR.
The narrative reflects in the gameplay, with a widely branching story and important choices throughout the game, that
affect your ending.
-VISUALS & PERFORMANCE:
The graphical fidelty in MD is pretty wild. The game is beautifully made and gameworld is rather believable; most buildings
have fully rendered interiors, even if you can't enter them. Some facial animations are a bit wonky, but it's nothing major.
It has a lot of settings, so you can pick exactly what works for you.
-VOICES & SOUND
Voice acting is really high quality. Additionally, many of the background NPC's in Prague speak Czech for increased immersion. Some of the english voice acting on the non-english characters can be a little cringy, but it's allright.
Sound design is fantastic, sound effects are impactful and believable. Music is composed by Michael McCann, who also composed the soundtrack for HR and it's great and immersive.
Overall,
is brilliant game, with tight gameplay and rewards creative thinking. Even when not playing on the hard difficulties, it is still a challenge. The ending is clearly setting up a continuation, which I am very much excited for.

The game is very in-depth with managing your country without sacrificing the military part of the game. The only thing that keeps it from a full 10 is that there is no editor for AoD like the first Hearts of Iron and the worst part is that the description is a lie. There is NO editor with the game nor is there a seperate editor tool, the only way to edit is the old fashioned way, screwing around with save game files using wordpad and/or notepad.
Even without a real editor however you can still accomplish a great deal with wordpad editing with hoi 1 and 2, something hoi 3 lacks is the freedom to edit with wordpad (most hoi 3 files, mainly the save games and scenario files, are   in a file format not compatable with wordpad.)
Overall it is better than the successor, hoi 3 in every way except map graphics, particularly because the regions in hoi 3 on the US dont take into account the accurate shape of the states where in all hoi games precedding, the states are accurately shaped by region and province shape.
They should remove from the list of features that (or at least rephrase it to point out that the files are wordpad editable instead of insinuating a non-existant editor) the hints of an editor that doesn't exist before someone decides to bash them with false advertisement OR solve the problem altogether by making an editor for AoD much like the first Hearts of Iron Scenario Editor which had an interactive map in which to set province ownership and the like.
If an editor exists for AoD then I would appreciate anyone messaging me or leaving a comment on my profile if the former is not possible with information on where to get it.
Aside from the lies about an editor however the game is great and is both historical and ahistorical as the AIs don't always make the same choices every game, meaning a lot of "what-if" scenarios can happen (Like the possibility of Germany mobilizing late, Stalin deciding not to purge his officers or Japan not attacking Pearl Harbor, though the major historical events the AI usually chooses the historical outcome often.)
So all in all, great game, 9 out of 10, if they put in a user-friendly editor to make the lies not lies, then it would be a 10, until they decide to do that however, it remains an imperfect yet high 9/10.
I highly reccomend this game with or without an editor due to the large array of choices you have at your disposal when managing your country (such as taking steps to turn america into a dictatorship, or being a non-insane hitler who focuses on the USSR instead of world domination or even playing as the Soviets and being the reason for WW2 instead of germany or even the very difficult yet still possible scenario where France doesn't become a cheese eating surrender monkey and actually fights the second world war.)

FC3: Blood Dragon is hard to describe. It's both a parody and a tribute of the 80's,  with a strange future timeline, based on the Far Cry 3 engine, and most of the same island. WIth a dark atmosphere you can't really tell it's the same island, and the neon decor (reminiscent of Tron) and the overly dramatic delivery of the heros, villains, and other characters, makes for one heck of a presentation.
You play Rex Power Colt, Mk IV Cybercommando of the US Military. Recently rebuilt / recovered from serious injuries and upgraded to Mk IV, you are sent with a buddy commando to infiltrate enemy compound to retrieve computer data... Only to discover the defending forces were commanded by your ex-commander, Colonel Sloan. However, you have someone helping you: Dr. Darling, someone forced to help Sloan develope this "dragon blood", which supercharged his cybernetics, making him more powerful than ever.
You start as a level 1. As you achieve objectives, make kills, and so on you will gain XP which will let you gain levels, and additional skills and additional health points. Max level is 30, and the progression table is fixed, i.e. you can't choose which power.
There are only so many weapons: pistol, assault rifle, sniper rifle, shotgun, minigun, blade, bow, grenade, molotox, mine, and C400 (satchel charge). But some weapons can be upgraded by attachments, which are unlocked through collecting collectibles.
The actual game mechanics are identical to Far Cry 3: take over outposts by killing everybody inside, preferably without being discovered. Once you liberate an outpost Scientists loyal to Dr. Darling will move in. You can still do takedowns, and you already know how to do takedown drag and chain takedowns, but the advanced moves like grenade takedown,  shuriken takedown, pistol takedown, as well as death from above, and death from below are activated later.
Animals are now mutated into strange forms, like cybercroc, cybershark, cyberpanther, etc. as well as tiger, cassowary, boar, goat, and more.
Then there's the game's namesake: blood dragon. Practically small dinosaurs, they also have some really fancy ability: shoot lasers out of their eyes. Yep. It's their blood that supercharged Sloan, and killing them can be extremely tough, but doable.
Scattered on the island are "TV Sets" that contains additional information about Omega Force, some "VHS Tapes" you have to 'rent' (i.e. collect) with horrible movie premises, and Dr. Darling's research notes. Collecting them unlocks weapon attachments that you can buy at the "vending machine" found in each outpost.
Much like Far Cry 3, you will find the scientists fighting with the Omega Force on the island, as well as with the creatures. It is up to you if you want to interfere.
Entire game is full of 80's pop culture references. You'll spot things from Star Wars, GI Joe, Aliens, and much much more. There's also jokes referring to other games, such as Far Cry 3, Assassin's Creed (collecting flags and feathers, hahahah), and much more.
Even the music is done in the 80's pop rock style.
And let's just say the beginning and ending are hilarious enough you may LOL or even ROFL. And it must be experienced in person. It can't really be explained.
All in all, Blood Dragon is a fun game with familiar mechanics, very different visuals, and callout to the 80's, and you should play it.

Absolutely a massively underated game. Yes its an xbox 360 port but with the new patch update and controller support, its quite beautiful in two ways. Graphically, yes its dated graphically but atmospherically it more than makes up for it. I personally really like the washed, sun bleached look. It all works brilliantly to be another character in itself. Bleak, dusty and desperate. You will stair in wonder at the sun glare and vista's through broken building windows, but despair about looking down to the dust soup below that you know you have to delve into.
The second positive is its combat is a really great attempt at different. You are taught to think about using the tools they give you with such an incredibly limited ammo supply, seriously limited. I have used the same one arrow for my bow in nearly every battle.
The added genius of a taunt option where you threaten with your pistol so that thugs back away at its sight and beg not be shot is great. However they will grow in confidence if you taunt to much and call your bluff realising that the gun is actually empty. Then they may attack, so will you machete, use the bow or run. You will die in this game, but each time it teaches you this is survival, so survive. It has a very standard but competent climbing and traversing mechanic which does its job well with good animation, although our hero does choose his own path occasionally.
If I have one gripe its that the save system is spread out quite a bit and when you have exhausted your in-between checkpoint tokens, gathered for saving civilians along the way, you will be sent back quite a way to a previous save point, and with this loose a lot progress that you may have made.
This game rewards exploration if you wish to risk it but with such intermitant saves points it also holds exploration back somewhat which is its only slight issue.
For a couple of pounds on steam, even if you pay a fiver i highly recommend this little gem. Think 'Shadow of the collosus' meets 'the last of us' and you are there.

I Am Alive might be one of the most ambitious and under-rated XBLA games of all time.
The niceties that are usually reserved for AAA gaming experiences are all present here. The soundtrack is stunning, the gameplay is innovative, and the atmosphere is remarkable.
That said, there are some problems with this game that do need to be addressed.
For one, there's a grainy filter that runs over the screen for the entire game. This isn't a glitch, but a purposeful design choice by the developers, presumably to make the game feel more gritty (or something). I don't quite understand the need for it, and it makes the game look pretty ugly.
There's also a stamina bar that slowly drains as you exert energy in the game, either by climbing buildings or traversing through the thick fog in the streets. When the bar gets about halfway down, the un-settling sound of shrieiking violins will fill your ears, indicating that your character doesn't have much longer to survive. This cranks the tension up to 11 during moments that might otherwise be a monotonous trudge, but by the 9th or 10th time it happens, you'll be looking for any excuse to avoid making your stamina drop. By the 50th time, you'll be taking off your headphones, setting them on your desk, and shaking your head in dissapointment. Sure, it's scary, and the sound sends chills up my spine, but there's no relief from it. That dreadful buzz will accompany nearly every moment of this game. It begins to feel like a cheap way to add horror into a game that really isn't that horrifying.
Other than that, I Am Alive is captivating. The "intimidation" style combat feels excellent and believeable. Enemies will cower under your gun while you're pointing at them, but if you don't shoot for an extended period, they'll start to think you're bluffing, and they'll rush you. If you shoot while you're out of bullets, enemies will take note of it, and seize the oppurtunity to slice you with their machetes. It's a decently in-depth system for a downloadable title, and it makes you seriously consider each encounter carefully.
Overall, I Am Alive is an impressive game. The story is simple, but well-told, and the character dialogue sounds natural. Shout-out to the voice actors as well, who do some amazing voiceovers for these characters. Their contribution to the game makes the world even more believable, and one that you'll want to get lost in.

Gnomoria is a detailed base-building game in which one pits a tribe of gnomes against evils from the depths of their mines and evils from other, invisible, villages.  Gnomes are able to mine a variety of resources, process them, and manufacture everything from furniture to armor.  They have to sleep, eat, and drink, and they can even become powerful zombies after death, returning later to slaughter any former friends that are caught unaware.
It's a fun game with plenty of opportunity for strategy and mayhem.
But, here's the thing: this game has been in Early Access forever, updates are slow, bug fixes are slow, and the game is using outdated technology (XNA, which was discontinued by Microsoft in early 2013) that doesn't even support some relatively common desktop features like 1440p resolution.
A year ago, I would have said Gnomoria is a hugely promising game and worth buying for double the price, but that's about when the developer slowed down.  A lot.  The game I was playing a year ago is very nearly the same game I could play today, were I to click the Play button again.
My advice: hit that "Follow" button on the store page, and if Gnomoria ever releases, give it another look.  I certainly will.

Trine 2 is a puzzle platformer and suited for those who like to relax their mind while playing a game. In Trine 2, you get to play with a warrior, archer and wizard with the ability to instantly switch among those classes. Warrior’s main use is to kill enemies, archer can swing from platforms that are otherwise very hard to reach , whereas the wizard conjures boxes and manipulates objects. The secondary goal (other than beating the mission) is to collect experience orbs which you can later use to distribute skill points to your characters.
The main selling point of Trine 2 is its astonishing graphics. The game is so good looking that you can basically take a random screenshot and use as wallpaper. Combined with the relaxing soundtrack and rather slow -think before you act- gameplay Trine 2 really calms you down every time you play it. Also, to get the most enjoyment out of it, you should play it coop online. Most missions show that the game was designed with coop play in mind.
However, the game is not without drawbacks.  Action is very shallow and you can kill most enemies by basic swings of sword. Also, the game is way too easy. I have played it in hard mode, yet did not come across any puzzles that took anytime to figure it out. With the added element of instant resurrection when you die and the ability of overcoming most puzzles with the alternative method of making box towers, the game offers almost zero challenge.  Other problems include bad storytelling (I have read everything and don’t really remember anything about the story) and some disconnection issues when playing online coop.
Finally, it was a bit of a surprise that despite being a side scroller puzzle platformer, Trine 2 is played best when played with a mouse + keyboard rather than a controller since aiming with the bow and creating boxes with the cursor are elements very often used during gameplay.
To sum up, Trine 2 is enjoyable while it lasts and beautiful to look at. But dull action mechanics and extremely easy gameplay might frustrate more experienced gamers.

PS: Play it coop, hard difficulty and with a keyboard.

Summary: A very fun, relatively short game to play alone or with friends. DLC is a must have if you enjoyed the classic game.
I played this game together with my girlfriend. Throughout our time playing this, she's mostly been playing Zoya (Mobile Archer), while i spent most of my time on Amadeus (Wizard). For fights I was the one to switch to Pontius (Knight). We had a ton of fun with the early puzzles, figuring out how our abilities worked and interacted, which they truly do quite a lot. The synergies between the characters are very rewarding to use and gives a true feeling of teamwork.
The story is quite straightforward, there isn't too much guessing or edge-of-your seat involved, you progressively find out more about what makes the world go 'round as you move forward in the game, so neither particularly good or bad.
Combat is rather simple, most of the time you will try to protect each other by moving obstacles, using shields or freezing enemies, other than that: smack 'em til dead. Sadly, boss fights are not particularly challenging with but a few dodge timings to keep in mind, major exception being the boss of the "Goblin Menace" DLC.
The DLC "Goblin Menace" spiced things up compared to the main game rather successfully. The puzzles were different, Fights more intriguing, particularly the last one, even cutscenes were polished up quite a bit. Definitely worth buying if you enjoy the Classic game!
Pros:
+ Teamwork-heavy game. helping each other complete puzzles or crossing terrain is mandatory and lends the game its charm.
+ beautiful graphics and artwork, every level and stage of the game is visually pleasing and has interesting details.
+ Sweet and rather innocent storyline, definitely suitable for younger players
+ Nice and bug-free, which is particularly apparent due to the many options you have to solve riddles, which can all work in their own way without having to abuse anything.
+ Short and pleasant game overall. The difficulty level can be adjusted to anything that suits you. We completed the game running on Medium in roughtly 12h total playtime.
Cons:

Despite that though, it is genuinely one of the most fun games I've ever played. (TL;DR at the end of review)
No matter how you cut it, this game is insanely repetitive. You'll probably play the same character over long periods, on the same maps in the same game modes.
The game is still fun. Despite this lack of variation, it remains fun. You could play the game for several hours and still be riding on that high you get from beginning to end. However, if you do play for long periods of time, this does become slightly more noticeable.
Yeah like any free to play game, it starts by showering you with rewards before dragging the process down to a pretty slow crawl. While not as bad as some games, it's still a bit of a turn off for people who don't want to be stuck with the same heroes for long periods of time. On the same note, You also don't start with any characters, which is kinda weird. I'm fine with it though as if you play well for a few hours a day, you can probably buy atleast 1 average priced character per week. The only solution I can offer to this, is just pick a main hero and save for it, and in the mean time just try out other characters. This will make the grind seem quicker and lead to less burnout.
I know I'm going to offend the hardcore fans when I say there isn't enough character variation, only gameplay wise though. Each character has unique stats, which at the end of the day feel as if they have no relevance, especially when most of the time it comes down to movement and combo knowledge. I mean why tell me my damage stat if there's no default healthbars? And then the only difference between each character is the weapons they use, but each class can use two and there are only like 7 in the game. Again,
, yet it feels like the devs put too much work into the behind the scene's stuff, when that time could be devoted elsewhere.
No it's not pay to win. There is not a single thing you can buy which will give you an advantage. But there are cosmetics (which is fine)... And there's alot of them... None of which can be earned in game. As far as I'm aware, there is no way to earn any cash shop items in game. Which sucks but that's clutching at straws honestly.
The game is insanely fun. Maybe even the most fun game I've ever played. Something about it is just addicting and enjoyable throughout. Not really much else to say here to be honest, just know if you play, you're almost guaranteed to have fun.
I went in expecting to dislike the visuals, but they eventually grew on me. Character designs are usually very unique and different to eachother visually, with some very good skins to go alongside them. The levels are wonderful. Each has a unique and beautiful background, all of which are great just to look at. Even the menu is stylised, yet simplistic making the whole game very simple to navigate yet still look great.
I know I'm in the minority when it comes to feeling as if the game is relatively samey and there isn't much variety. The devs however are working on it so kudos to them. The game is constantly updated, with new heroes, skins and modes being added at a decent pace. Eventually, I feel as if I'll be able to retract some of my statements, but for now my critiscism still stands.
This seems like a weird thing to put in the good section, but it is. It means that this game has alot of potential. I feel as if the game is insanely polished already, to the point where I didn't realise it was in Beta until long into my time playing. I feel as if the game could release fully today and that would be fine as it's of very high quality already. However, the devs go higherand higher with this game, constantly tweaking and updating the game, trying to increase the content base of the game, which is fantastic conduct.
TL:DR; Great game, insanely fun, fast paced gameplay. F2P and very balanced. It's in early access but is polished to the point you wouldn't even realise it. Not to mention the potential for this game is great, and it's on track to becoming one of steam's greatest games.

Okay, so when was the last time you picked up a game nowadays and there wasn't shooter mechanics involved? Batman: Arkham Asylum just so happens to be proof that the action-adventure genre can still survive and do extraordinarily well in terms of profit amidst a plethora of other games that do the same old thing all over again. A lot of the gameplay reminds myself of older adventure games, and mixes it up with brawler action stuff which is good, but those with less than an average competence with button-press timing may find that the flow of combat is often interrupted and can at times be infuriating. The narrative is pretty much standard Batman with the twist that you face multiple of his most notorious villains, with Joker being a sort of pseudo-kingpin with a master plan. Add on the voice talent of Kevin Conroy and Mark Hamill reprising  their roles as Batman and Joker respectively, and you definitely feel like this is an authentic Batman experience. All in all, if you haven't played Arkham Asylum by now, you really REALLY should, as it is (and was) a refreshing change of pace to the usual product.
P.S. Kudos to whomever was in charge of putting those collectibles in the right places. Solving a puzzle to get the shiny thing is way more rewarding than just running around everywhere to find a feather perched at the top of a random building.

I would say this game is at least a 7/10. It has an innovative combat system, to were if you aim a gun at someone who has no ranged weapon they will put their hands up, and this means that if there is a fire or cliff nearby, you can kick them into it. However, this gets clunky, and while ammo is scarce if you only pick it up yourself, shoot an enemy that has a gun and  you get your ammo back. A true flaw that feels lazy and unfinished is the story. Your nameless, however not silent protaganist will trust the sketchiest of characters, and the ending doesn't tie up loose ends. It feels as if it was unfinished, or that the studio was going to make a sequel and decided not to do it. Another gripe I have with the game is the stamina. It runs out when you climb, even when standing still on a ledge, which I know from experience is that is not true, and when you are in this "Heavy Fog" as they call it. It's just a lot of dust, and when in it, your stamina goes down, too.  Sure, a dust cloud would impair your breathing, but it wouldn't kill you if you were just walking in it.  I did enjoy playing it, but I want more out of it. It did feel a bit unfinished, and in this review I spoke mostly to the negetives, but if you get this game, you would find that there are plenty of positives, too. So. a great game, just with some glaring flaws. Or at least that's my take on it.

Bought this game when it was on sale for Halloween. For three dollars, yeah it'd be worth it. For full price? No.
In short, it's very simplistic and feels very lazy. The characters are laughably simplistic with very little background ever established... which would really help given the main character seems to have the skillset of an Assassin from the Assassin's Creed franchise. I really would like to know how he's able to scale bridges and parkour on the level he does.
For a game about survival in a post-apocalyptic world there's very little actual survival and more on-rails walking engagement to engagement. You can't scavenge from the rubble, can't check inside containers or trash cans. This by itself hurts immersion.
What totally kills the immersion is the fact that even the fights are puzzles. You have to kill certain enemies in certain ways and in a certain order or you're dead before you know it. Stranger still is the ability to carry just one bullet for your magazine-fed handgun. There's no simple melee, no way to counter someone running up on you and no way to grapple someone less than a foot away from you with a firearm.
Even the animations are lazy. There's a scene wherein the main character is carrying a child on his back and ends up having to use his machete to break a chain. Our hero then sheaths this machete into the child's character model.
In conclusion? Boring, frustrating and not worth it. For a much better urban survival experience I'd reccomend the Fallout franchise.

After about an hour of playing this game, here is my view of it:

-wise, it's extremely white/bright and has that horrible grain effect that doesnt let you fully enjoy the beauty of the map that isn't actually there.

-wise, The audio was all over the place. I suppose the support for 5.1/7.1 surround sound was horribly done in the game, because any people that talked were always somewhere else than from where the sound was coming from.

-wise, the controls are a little irritating, and for me, getting the camera to move at all was a challenge. I would be dragging my mouse across my entire desk just for the game to recognise that I wish to turn
. This may just be me, but it made it un-playable and ruined the game within the first 5 minutes.

-wise, absolutely lazy. Ammo is extremely scarce, from what i've seen
, you constantly have only one bullet at your disposal. The only way to melee people is to get up-close and personal to them. while everyone is attempting stabbing you in the sides, you gotta walk up and press 'E' to attack.
.

-wise, somewhat enjoyable. Even though the start is a bit cheesy, the story seems to have more pontential than anything else in the game. While only an hour in, however, I can't say much about it.

-wise, there are almost no customization settings what-so-ever. In the video settings, you can change the brightness, the resolution, the aspect ratio, anti-aliasing, the graphic quality itself
, FXAA, or VSync. This menu leaves you no room to really adjust the graphics for that 'high quality' look. The audio settings is just the volumes of main, music, voice, and sound effects. This doesn't bother me as much, but I was hoping for some options for surround-sound, coming from a semi-stealth game.
Overall I would say this game is about a 4/10 from my view of it within an hour of game-time. I may be missing more good things or bad things about the game, but so far this game wasn't worth it.

Fourth:It achives everythig it sets out to do almost perfectly.
Ziggurat is a fast paced shooter that takes betweeb 1-3 hours to complete. The game (like all roguelikes) gets its value from replays. New characters, weapons and items are unlocked after each playthrough. to keep repetition being an issue, the levels are made out of a random selection of premade rooms. The enemy placement is also different every time. There are even chalange rooms the has a certian condition that has to be meet or an effect in the room. Examples include: Totems that need to be destroyed before the player can move on, enemies that is small or platforming levels filled with traps. To get out of a room the player has to kill all the "minions". The enemies include Lost Soul like enemies, skeletal knights and killer carrots. The shooting is very fast and hectic. It reminds me of Hexen.
TLDR: Amazing rouge-like. Great graphics. The gameplay is very reminiscent of the Hexen games.
P.S. Most of Hexen's cheats works on Ziggurat.

So I've read a lot of reviews with Mankind Divided.
A lot has been criticised and I want to touch base onto the exaggeration of people's opinions/reviews of the game.
I want to point out the game is good if you have played Deus 1 through to now.
It answers a lot of questions that you question in the older games. It gives you clues and answers to how the turmoil of human augmentation began from human revolution and how the story leads up to the events with JC Denton in the older games.
You are given the first look of bob page and Manderly conspiring for world control.
I liked this. It's setting up a even stronger story for the next addition to the series.
As others have written, it lacks content.
This is true. After around 10-15 hours of gameplay Prague is boring and you revisit areas you have already been through.(hacking, using multi tools, ventilation etc) to gain access everywhere. If you are a deus ex veteran you know levelling hacking is one of the first things to do.
This really annoyed me. Human evolution was great separating the cities.
Different weapons where slowly introduced and praxis kits where balanced. Especially when you lost your praxxis points mid game and had to redistribute your praxis points. These quirky surprises added dynamics to the game. Mankind didn't have any of this. It felt bland.
In Prague you could literally do all the side missions first and explore and hack while using non lethal take downs to gain big xp. If you did this like I did it made the main missions very easy have a overwhelmingly higher amount of skills levelled.
There weren't really any new weapons that were very different. They also removed a lot of weapon mods that existed in HR.
Crafting was cool though.
Graphically the game is stunning. Not very well optimised though. I could barely get 60fps on my 1080.
Gameplay is ok. The quick menu is still clunky like the other games but I don't see a fix for it. To be honest it makes a deus ex game.
The tactical mechanics are good. The map layouts are also good.
You are given multiple options on how you can deal with your enemy.
I rate the game 7/10
Grab deus ex 1 and human revolution to get a better understanding of the story first then buy this.

This game is really amazing, I have been very impressed so far in the first 7 hours.  It's kind of open world, you collect missions, but can go do whatever for the most part. I was suppose to go meet this guy at his shop on the first mission. I get side tracked and run around. End up crawling thru a series of random vents into this mob safehouse with tons of loot and alarms everywhere. It ended up leading to a side mission and then later I went and did some main missions. Being able to play it that way was a lot of fun.
The visuals are really amazing and the game runs very smooth. Nearly maxed out with an rx 480 @ 1080p 60fps. Not a single crash in 7 hours. The fps is very solid as well, no dips or stuttering. The ability to interact with basically everything is nice. You can pick up or move almost anything in the game. There are also multiple paths and various ways to do things. You can go rooftops, sewers, windows and around ledges, etc... You can play stealthy or all out explosive warrior.
The only negative would be the cover system and some of the combat feels a little funky. I don't wanna say it's bad, it just feels like it's going to take a while to really get use to it. Moving from cover to cover and then popping up to shoot is not the smoothest thing. It works pretty well if your playing stealth, but if your trying to do these things quickly it can be a bit complicated. It's far from game breaking and I think after 8-10 hours of gameplay I'll have it down to a point where I can compensate for these things. I'm really picky about games with clunky combat, but this isn't that bad, it's just the only real negative I've found so far.
I really like how everything 100% stops when you open up the item wheel, special ability wheel or inventory. You don't have to worry about trying to swap between 20 different things constantly while the action only gets slowed down instead of stopping completely. The last Deus Ex only slowed down and I hated that part of it. The upgrade system is pretty sweet and they have tons of mods / abilites. If you like the story there seems to be a ton of it with lots of cut scenes / dialogue. I personally can't stand lots of cut scenes in most games, but this one is done very well.
Game is way too difficult even on easy. Too many enemies that absorb bullets like a sponge. I play many styles of game but this is just annoying.

Only realized too late when game stopped creating new saves. Even unable to load autosaves. I absolutely cannot recommend buying this game until the bug is officially fixed. This is a problem that ANY player will be bound to encounter. It is an agonizing experience to lose time and effort. A massive turn off from wanting to play again. Could they not code the game to detect failure to save on the Steam cloud, and automatically fall back to saving on the local drive? Even a simple fix like that could not be made in half a year? Negligent AND incompetent!
Recommended.

Forget everything else. It's when I listen to Isaac roar as he stomps his armored boot three times on the corpse of a necromorph, shattering it to bloody ribbons, and seething out "S***! F***! Die!" that I truly appreciate this game. I love nothing more than a game that understands the importance of being able to not just kill, but brutally, viscerally decimate enemies in appallingly violent and unnecessary ways. Isaac Clarke is not a steel-nerved soldier who stoically keeps his cool at every ounce of fresh hell. He's a hard-edged engineer desperately trying to stay alive, using jury-rigged industrial power tools for weapons. He lives and breathes and savors every little victory he can. The fact that the game both manages to convey this so well, and that it provides plenty of tense challenges for Isaac to overcome, is what really sold it for me. 5/5, totally recommended, get this glorious piece of art for your library!

Pros:

-SALT

Brawlhalla is a great game to play with your friends or on free-for-all, but on ranked things can get pretty crazy and dumb depending on who you're up against(because SALTY PEOPLE), but other times people just don't say anything. It can take awhile to unlock characters, but it's worth it if you're willing to play this a lot. You should definitely get this game and tell all of your friends who love Super Smash Bros. I would also advise you to NOT BUY the $20 character pack because then it ruins a lot of the experience(Valhalla Pack is fine though). Highly recommend using controller, but I've met some people that can pull of the game using keyboard so choose what works best for you.

Batman: Arkham Asylum. Am Anfang denkt man sich: "Ach, wieder so ein blödes Superhelden-Prügelspiel, das eh keine gescheite Story hat!", aber das ist es eben nicht. Arkham Asylum ist eines der besten Superhelden-Spiele, die ich je gespielt habe, und mein Gott habe ich viele Superhelden-Spiele gezockt. Ich liste euch mal die Pros und Kontras auf:
Pros:
- Extrem geile Grafik, bei der sich sogar der Rauch teilt, wenn eine Figur hindurchläuft
- Wundervolle Story mit vielen Wendungen
- Das Spiel verbreitet ein tolles Batman-Flair
- Sehr abwechslungsreich, u.a. Stealth-Abschnitte, bei denen ihr nicht entdeckt werden dürft, oder viel Detektivarbeit mit dem Detektivscanner. Richtig spaßig!
- Gute Steuerung, auch mit Maus und Tastatur (Ich empfehle trotzdem ein Gamepad, da die Prügelabschnitte so einfach leichter verlaufen)
- Viele Riddler-Rästel, die euch noch viele Stunden unterhalten können
P.S.: Highscore-Jäger können sich auch an die Herausforderungen machen
Contras:
- Die Detektivarbeit ist nur sehr selten, und wenn, dann auch nur sehr kurz.
- Nur wenige Gadgets (Batarang, Batclaw, Line Launcher etc.)
- Der Endkampf ist etwas zu leicht
Fazit: Wenn ihr Superhelden mögt, ist Arkham Asylum exakt das Richtige für euch. Auch Action-Fans kommen auf ihre Kosten. Man muss sich auch mal trauen, was auszuprobieren, denn wenn man dieses Spiel nicht spielt, verpasst man eines der besten Action-Adventures aller Zeiten. Wer immer noch nicht überzeugt ist, der solle sich doch bitte die Demo von dem Spiel auf chip.de runterladen.

It has its flaws (some bugs, terrible lags in spome places, somtimes unbalanced in pvp after some updates) but I think it is very good game.
Some very nice features of the game:
- Middel-earth shown in very detailed form (from green fiels of Shire, trought deeps of Moria and dark woods of Mirkwood, near towering Orthanc to plains of Rohan and Gondor ... and beyond ;). Thats just few places that you may explore in LOTRO.
- Early books of main quest and some side quest are very intresting and tell us some orginal tale. Later is worse and story stick more to the books (but ist very lorelike).
- Looks - charcters and their outfit system and later also war-steed outfits. One person once said when you look good you fight good ^^
- unique pvp system - in fact pvmp - player vs monster player. Very nice region to fight players of the opposite side. Game mostly is build around cooperative fight of forces of free people against hordes of Sauron and his servants/slaves/allies but in Ettenmoors (and Osgiliath) you may fight as one of the orcs/uruks/spiders/wargs against other "good" players or opposite (* to play as one of the free people you need to be VIP or buy special pass (for 6hr)).
- nice instances (dungeons) and raids. Some of them are very uniqe. Generally LOTRO is not very hard game to play but has its own chellenges.
- length - if you want to dive for long hours in MIddel-Earth then ist for you
- nice housing system for your personal house and kinship house (kinship=guild)
- good crafting system
- mounted combat (since Rohan) you may fight from your horse. For me it is great thing I really liked and most of my friends but generally has some flaws and is not liked by most of the community (pity)
- Wonderful music - really great soundtrack is in this game.
- nice community
Of course such big game has its flaws:
- Lag in some places is terrible (especially in high burrning areas of Gondor near Minas Tirith)
- Lack of scaling system (there is item that you may buy to prevent gaining experience so you wont level too fast - otherewise some part of game can become to easy). The scaling system appears only in Big Battels (one type of instances that are in lotro). Since it exist in one part ist pity it is unaviable for normal gameplay or other type of instance or raids.
- Like in all mmos there is a bit of grinding at the end game content
- some problematic bugs that appear after last expansion but I hope they fix them soon
Summary
Even with its flaws LOTRO is great game and I recommend it for all Middel-earth fans.

A neutral review. As of 25/05/2015
The game has been in development for years and frankly it still needs years given the current progress being made before it's ready for release in my opinion. A fun ride but it's very bumpy.
The cons.
1. Some crashes still exist (although I haven't been plagued with them myself)
2. Pathfinding is awkward at best due to the next problemVVV
3."Fail states" exist, if you deconstruct a well sometimes the gnomes bug out trying to pick up the deconstructed parts or something. Or if you mine in the "wrong" way you can isolate your miners who eventually die of thirst, thus killing your colony before it even begins.
4. Lack of information about what things do. It's hard to know when it's a good time to "tech" up and when the build defenses, do I want extra armour? I don't know. Do I want to fight that bear? I don't know.
5. Learning curve is steep and doesn't show signs of slowing down after 14 hours of play. Yes this is a con.
6. Under constant attack, dealing with constant attacks from things gets annoying, and feels like i'm on firefighting duty rather than building a colony or town.
7. Combat system is bad sad bad, lots of little things you can forget can bite you in the behind later on. The lack of individual control over the gnomes feels especially frustrating here.
8. Animations are incredibly lacking if even present. Understandable but not acceptable.
9. Camera view is awkward. Not a huge problem but at times it becomes a hindrance being stuck in diagonal view.
Pros.
1. Very satisfying figuring out problems and optimising things.
2. Lots of replayability, if you can figure out the issues with the game it's not that bad to play.
3. Balancing what to build and when is quite fun, and is probably one of the main reasons people play the game. Just because I haven't figured out the optimal way doesn't mean you can't.
4. Customisation options are quite varied, provided you can survive long enough to reach them.
5. The game is still being worked on despite being several years in the works which says something about the dedication of the developers.
6. Lots of ways to play the game...after a certain point.
7. You have a lot of control over how the gnomes behave, granted the interface for controlling them is very very awkward, you do technically have a lot of say over how they behave.
Conclusion clunky controls, annoying combat mechanics and general lack of polish means this game should be avoided until it's complete.
Lack of information to the player and any real feedback on what they're doing increases the learning time required to get the basics understood.
Proceed at your own risk to investment in time.

AoD focuses very much on domestic and economic issues (repairing provinces, civic investment as a means to alleviating dissent as opposed to simply cranking out consumer goods). To use the technology tree as an example -- colors seem stark and non-period while useability refinements such as historical years within each tech's respective title should have been implimented. The AI also makes questionable ahistoric decisions, leaving history-minded players stuck. If you're open-minded and wanting unpredictablity though, that might be right up your alley.
All that being said, I recommend this to players wanting diplomatic and policy-heavy gameplay without losing military action.

This is a great Diablo-style game. Many people consider it to be a better game than Diablo 3. I don't go that far for a few reasons, but I can understand why people (specially Diablo 2 veterans) would think that.

- Amazingly fluid combat system, very satisfying to kill stuff
- Enjoyable visuals if you don't mind it being very cartoony

- Amazing steam workshop full of mods. My personal favorite is the mod that exchanges the sounds for Diablo 2 sound effects. Ah, the nostalgia.
- Simple yet effective character building based on skill trees and point distributions - just like Diablo 2
- Instead of mercenaries, you have a pet. You can like, have a pug as your merc.
- Amazing soundtrack by the same composer of the D2 soundtrack
- Runs on pretty much any pc
- Accessible, budget option.
Cons:
- Dead multiplayer unless you got friends to play with you.
- No ladder or any other form of competitive multiplayer. If you want that, go play Path of Exile
- Short game

- Generates way too much loot, itemization is a little messy

I really wanted to give this game a try, but it seems to be fighting back.
There is NO FOV SETTING in the game, so if you tend to suffer from motion sickness induced by low FOV, this is not your game. There are hacks available, though. On the plus side, the game does not appear to have motion blur.
There are several issues with the game, such as the controls not remappable separately, but only as a group (e.g. "Drop/Draw Weapon"). And since "Fire" and "Run" are in the same group, that is really annoying.
Another issue (and ultimately the one that leads me to not recommending the game) is that the game streams in world data, and when it does that, it sometimes stops responding to mouse input. This can go away within moments, but on occasion it stays. As a result, your mouse cursor will be fixed to the centre of the screen, in menus as well as in Windows when tabbed out. Even killing the game process doesn't seem to fix it, only a system reboot will do.

This game is really just full of unique features that you won't find in most other games of the post-apocalyptic survival category.
Other notes: the graphics are just good; not excellent, not average, but just good. The sounds reinforce the game's atmosphere pretty well. The AI can be tough to deal with at times. The level design itself is a puzzle at times.
Again, if you are looking for an interesting post-apocalyptic singleplayer game to play, this could be the game for you. If you want something more action oriented or roleplay-ish, you might want to skip this one. This game gets a 7/10 from me.

I am glad I got this on sale for 15.00, because at full price, this would be a rip-off. DO NOT PAY FULL PRICE FOR THIS GAME!
The game itself looks nice, but there are a lot of issues here, even harder to overlook as this is a AAA title so we should expect it to be great.
Technically the game has issues. I spent more time recovering from crashes than playing in some areas of the game. From an indie and/or single dev. game this may be easier to overlook, even more on a fun game. For a company that is now international and has 41M in the bank, this is just unacceptable. They basically get the players to do their QA for them. Cost effective in the short term this type of nonsense is hitting their bottom line. It is clear they have lost the vision and direction of what made them great in the first place, namely making great games for the PC. Typical BS when so called executives and managers are hired that have no love for the product.
The gameplay itself is mediocre and often I found myself having to push through to finish, rather than enjoying the ride. The levels are small and cramped, and very linier. The game leads the player around by the nose and your choices make no difference. The augmentations are barely used, and why not the battery life is shorter than a few seconds and the bio-gel is used up so fast, we may have just as well been running around with a backpack of AA batteries. The weapons are a joke, you only end up using a few and they feel like toys. The new ‘augs’ are completely useless with the exception being remote hacking - which is still barely useful. There is a whole lot of time filler so the time played is about the 30-35 hours with completion of all quests. In reality there is about 15 hours tops of game play.
The plot-line is terrible, disjointed and full of holes half the characters are not needed and the ones that are, are flat and are forgettable. They use every trope in the video-game book making it feel old and tired and overall BORRING.
The voice acting was sub-par, I wanted to find and shoot the TV announcer! She is ever-present blabbing on over and over the same things on an endless loop. Since there are monitors everywhere, you never can get away. Even worse, the acting sounds like the IT intern was asked to read it, it was so poorly acted.
Get your S**T together Eidos, you have jumped the shark and are heading for a Titanic ending!

DLC Quest is a satire of the current state of the videogame industry.
Many games today often sell expansions, DLC, season passes, micro transactions, and so on added to the base game which is $60 on release. This often allows developers and publishers to cut content in order to sell it later.
DLC Quest makes fun of this stigma by collecting coins in order to unlock the basics such as the ability to jump, hear sound, obtain cosmetics, encounter the true ending of the game, and so forth.
The game is short and humorous that often reminds people how crappy the current state of the videogame industry is in today.
9/10.

It seems rare to find games that are this intricately detailed, and clearly lovingly crafted. It's rarer that these games are free.
Mandagon is a short experience, but if you ever find yourself with an hour in the afternoon, let yourself enjoy the serene soundtrack and find your way through the temple door.

+ Beautiful art
+ Calming
- Silly storytelling
This is a nice, relaxing little game to play. Mandagon is an extremely basic platformer with no threat from enemies or obstacles. The closest it gets is falling in the water between platforms, which only necessitates climbing back out again using a geiser. It's much easier to move upwards than to return to places below on foot, but the tablets you collect allow you to teleport back to ones you've previously activated, which is a good anti-frustration feature.
The story is told by  statues sprinkled throughout the level that speak in rhyming couplets, which feels unnecessary and breaks the isolated, contemplative atmosphere the game otherwise maintains through its beautiful art and chill music. I also wish the world had a tiny bit more variation in its design to keep the different areas of the singular level more distinct, but it's a pleasant place to visit for the half-hour or so it takes to complete a run.

The game is really, really beautiful, as you can see from the screenshots!
Even though it looks a bit crude (looks jagged in movement, some patterns seem a bit flattened, etc.), there are tons of intricate patterns I really like!
The music is a bit strange, with some details I enjoyed (the birds and bells, for example), but I wasn't aware of it, for the most part. So yeah, wasn't good nor bad, for me.
The game itself is the worst part, since, despite a beautiful and rather large "world" (the game is short, it's only "large" in the context of a single room/level), it's just about jumping on platforms and using lifts to get to several tablets spread around the game.
The platforming isn't challenging at all (you're quite slow in the air), and most of the jumps are very forgiving, giving you a fair window for error.
There are no mechanics at all, other than a single jump.
So yeah, you can imagine it being very stale. It's just about moving around, with the most basic movement system you could think of.
The only challenge here is orientation, since the game only lets you see the map in specific spots, so you can get lost, or miss something and forgetting where it might have been.
The other aspect I should mention is the whole "Tibetan theology/philosophy". I think what they wanted to say was "imagery", because there's nothing meaningful about philosophy or theology here. And nothing apparently that relates to a particular way of thinking.
There are some cryptic lines spread around the game, but you never have to use or understand them. So... no.
Maybe there are some environmental clues I'm missing? Maybe... but even if there are, they're completely isolated from the *game*, making them irrelevant.
If it was just about imagery, well... they should set different expectations in the description, I guess.
The game isn't too bad, and it's free, so nothing's stopping you from giving you a go.
I just didn't find anything interesting in it aside from the art-style, so I'll give it a no.
I'm interested in their future projects regardless! With more experience, something better may come!

At a glance, Who's Your Daddy might look like just another one of those garbage games that somehow passed through greenlight - but unlike most of those games, Who's Your Daddy is actually surprisingly fun. The game's concept is fairly simple, in which one player plays as a baby and tries to kill themself using a variety of household objects, while the other player controls a dad trying to protect the baby, providing a shockingly realistic portrayal of actual parenthood. There are a variety of ways for the baby to kill themself, like eating batteries or dropping a toaster in the sink, giving the game replayability by challenging yourself to kill yourself in creative ways. The dad gets various objects to try to protect the baby, like a tool to lock drawers and a baby grabbing handle to temporarily pick up the baby, and can also do chores around the house to get powerups like Dad Bod, which allows you to carry heavier things. The game is only in alpha right now, but the developer seems to be fairly diligent in adding regular updates that add new features and ways to die, and at five dollars per copy I think it's a pretty good game to get together with a friend and have a few hours of laughter.

A worthy addition to the Deus Ex series.
Improves on Human Revolution in almost every way. The level design was solid in HR but here it feels much more organic and natural, like these are real places. Prague is AMAZING, one of the best city hubs in an immersive sim with countless hidden secrets and corners to explore. There are many more different ways to interact with the world from physics to noise to manipulating the world around you: remote hacking is great... turn on a TV or radio from outside a room and watch a guard go in to investigate then sneak past quietly or pounce on them when they come out. And there's no more unavoidable boss battles that force you to break your play style.
They clearly learned a lot from Human Revolution.
The story is mostly good. I think it misses out on explaining a few things (like Jensen's connection with Juggernaut) but it builds on the world established in the previous game, gradually ramping up the intrigue, and links back to the original series in various neat ways. It adds some cool new characters (Rucker, Marchenko, Daria Mishka) though some are underutilized. I wanted to find out more about Aria and Chikane and see more of Sarif. It's cool to see Pritchard return in the DLC, but I missed Malik.
Great side missions! If you only do the main story you are missing out. The Harvester detective mission and the drug trafficking underground were some highlights. Also I was impressed with the multiple major paths offered at crucial points (like going for the Church of the Machine God or the bank heist).
People need to stop whining about the ending. Without spoiling anything, the ending is fine. It wraps up the main thread of the story in a tense climactic finale, while also clearly building to a sequel and towards the events of the original Deus Ex (set in 2052). This is very much the middle game in a trilogy. It's going to leave a few questions and mysteries open.
Stunning art direction, from the design of the city and its people to the oppressive Utelek ghetto... and oh man, Prague by night in the rain under curfew by the light of police cars is really something!
The music is also good, though it's hard to surpass the incredibly memorable Icarus theme from Human Revolution. It's more ambient, but it suits the game.
DLC: I've played Desperate Measures, System Rift and Criminal Past. The first two feel like side-missions. I don't have a problem with these being paid DLC (they are worth getting) but I do wish that, like Mass Effect and Witcher 3 DLC, they would be integrated into the main game once purchased instead of being standalone stories. They both take place during the events of the main story and would have fit more elegantly as missions that you get from NPCs in the main hub and then take the subway to go their locations. Of the two, System Rift is the most substantial.
Criminal Past is more of a standalone story (framed as a flashback), and bigger than the other two. New location, very different vibe (with the undercover prison angle), good expansion.
CONCLUSION : A solid immersive sim that continues the series in style. If you liked Human Revolution you'll enjoy this.

At a glance, Who's Your Daddy might look like just another one of those garbage games that somehow passed through greenlight - but unlike most of those games, Who's Your Daddy is actually surprisingly fun. The game's concept is fairly simple, in which one player plays as a baby and tries to kill themself using a variety of household objects, while the other player controls a dad trying to protect the baby, providing a shockingly realistic portrayal of actual parenthood. There are a variety of ways for the baby to kill themself, like eating batteries or dropping a toaster in the sink, giving the game replayability by challenging yourself to kill yourself in creative ways. The dad gets various objects to try to protect the baby, like a tool to lock drawers and a baby grabbing handle to temporarily pick up the baby, and can also do chores around the house to get powerups like Dad Bod, which allows you to carry heavier things. The game is only in alpha right now, but the developer seems to be fairly diligent in adding regular updates that add new features and ways to die, and at five dollars per copy I think it's a pretty good game to get together with a friend and have a few hours of laughter.

Ziggurat is an absolutely fantastic first person dungeon-crawler shooter! I can honestly say that it doesn't do too many things wrong, but it definitely does SO many things right.
The game plays as a rogue-like, so the power ups, items, dungeon layouts, etc will all change for
So here's the Upside:
- The sense of speed is phenomenal and combines well with good maneuverability.
- There is a decent amount of auto-aim so that the game doesn't become too frustrating with the difficulty.
- The weapons are variable and plentiful, with even more to be unlocked.
- There are 4 categories of weapons: Wand (always have), Staves, Spell Books, and Alchemic Weapons.
- It's fairly easy to keep your weapon meters full and ready to use.
- While there is a bit of a learning curve for sure, the challenge of becoming better is very rewarding and inviting.
Ex: Upon dying, you'll wrack up points that will unlock new abilities and upgrades at random. These upgrades can be  found randomly within the dungeon or earned by leveling up.
- Speaking of upgrades, I enjoyed how you were given 3 at random upon leveling up, but certain upgrades allowed for more options or to pick more than one.
- I enjoyed how every floor of the dungeon had a randomized boss usually chosen from 3 different
potential bosses with their own arenas and gimmicks.
- Another enjoyable feature were that not all rooms were used for spawning and fighting enemies.
Ex: There are enemy rooms, trap rooms, puzzle/treasure rooms, shrine rooms, and the
occasional hidden room.
- The game has a good balance of platforming and fighting as a result of these various types of rooms.
- When it comes to unlockables, there are TONS of characters, each with very customized starting builds to keep the experience fresh as you go along, as well as unique challenges for unlocking them.
Ex: Some have more speed but less defense, some are more suited to staves or spell books or
even the basic wand, some may gain experience faster.
- Lastly, a very cool feature they included is a daily challenge that everyone can compete in. Everyone has the same wizard from the beginning and the goal is just to go as far as you can before dying. Then, you're posted on a leaderboard for that day.
Downside:
- The types of enemies are not the most plentiful, but they do a good job of using various enemies at once when fighting.
- The learning curve can be a bit too much for many people.
- While "easy" is too easy, "normal" is considerably harder.
- There can be the issue of packing too many enemies into too small a room, thus making it more likely that you'll die.
- Due to the randomness of the upgrades and types of magic you find, you may end up having a poor run due to not getting   enough of the proper upgrades you need or the right types of spell books, staves, alchemic weapons, etc.
Overall, the game is a wonderful experience that is worth the money. It has great replayability because there's always someone or something to unlock, but the process of learning and becoming better is also greatly rewarding. When you make it to the next floor you feel accomplished, but finally completing the game feels amazing. The controls are smooth, the graphics are enjoyably Alice-esque, and the upgrades and weapons are so diverse, creative, and random that you are guaranteed to have to play on your toes as each new experience with a new procedurally generated dungeon demands new strategies.
Final Notes:
- Great challenge
- Great reward

I can handle all of that, but the bosses are my biggest problem: they're just regular enemies scaled up. That's so boring! If they'd only pushed it a little further it could've been excellent, but as things are I just give this game "it's fine." Can't say I don't recommend it, but can't super say I do.

The demand on your time can be as little or as much as you want.  If you're away from the game for a few days your cities will be fine (most likely).  If you're worried about that and you have made a couple trusts worthy friends in game they can sit your account for you until you return.  Once you have settled a couple cities and have built them up there is so much you can do with diplomacy (mostly spying), building, researching, crafting, selling, and , oh yes, war.
The mechanics work and are deeply layered in this game.  You can't learn it all in one sitting but if you take it a little at a time you'll eventually understand.  Nothing is very complicated but there are many simple mechanics at work with most in game activities.  A key thing that you must learn is that TEAM WORK is the backbone of this game.  Not graphics,  micro transactions, celebrity voice acting, nor unique game play... Its team work.
Which brings me to community.  Illyriad has an outstanding community.  It is so full of helpful and friendly players.  When I first started I was given a very sizable shipment of goods just for asking a question in global chat.  There are a lot of charitable people in this game.  However there are some who are not so.  There are militarily aggressive alliances as well as peaceful training alliances. Both have their place and I enjoy a world that allows me to construct these intricate cities but also presents a reality where they could be under threat.  I'm not trying to write a guide but I do urge new players to research the player alliances and pick the best one for you.
I think most people that give up the game or who don't like it are ones that tried to go at it alone.  People sometimes complain that there is no real PvP.  That is a complete lie.  There are always attacks going on.  And if you want that PvP you can have it.  The problem is if you go at it alone and choose your targets carelessly then you will be confronted with the awesome might of one or more of these alliances.  That's not the work of the dev's.  That's the community.  If you can't accept that, then this game may not be for you.

If you previously didn't own this game due to GFWL, now is your chance to get your hands on what is, without a doubt, the definitive superhero game.

If you like Batman this is an absolute must play, but even if you don't I'd highly recommend it based on its merits as a masterpiece of gaming.

Before going into why I cannot recommend this game, let me point out that there are a couple of positive aspects to Illyriad.  First, for a MMO, the game's community is exceedingly welcoming to newcomers.  Many of the established players are willing to answer basic questions in the chat, and even provide early game resource donations.  The game world is suitably large and there is a strategic depth to the game that requires classic "guns vs. butter" decision making.
Those things said, there are two components of the game that prevent a recommendation.
There is absolutely a P2W aspect to the game.  It's not overbearing, but it is there.  There are time gates to facets of the game; things such as building construction, resource gathering, trade and others all occur in real time.  If you want to avoid the wait, you can "rush" the completion of these tasks by spending Prestige (the in game currency that is available for purchase).
Of course, one can play the game in such a way that rushing construction and so forth doesn't make too big of a difference.  If you are of the mind that you simply wanrt to develop a network of varied cities, conduct research, gather resources and so forth without engaging in the PvP, you can certainly do so (so long as one of your more established neighbors doesn't get itchy and decide you are a prime target).  However, that brings up the second critical flaw.
As you constuct your initial city, you will be able to research certain technologies that allow for varied buildings and units.  This is all worthwhile as it forms the foundations of what your city can produce.  However, once you have progressed enough to settle a second city (and start thinking about the new tenor this city will possess) you are met with the fact that you have to start all research over again.  In other words, even though you researched the Militia technology in the first city (a necessity), you have to research it again in your new city.  Seeing as the object of the game is to create and foster an integrated kingdom, this mechanic makes absolutely no sense and is unnecessarily frustrating.
In the end, if you are looking to engage in the social aspect of a MMO, Illyriad is probably as good a choice as any other.  However, if you are looking for a game that provides a sense of progression and proportionate reward for effort, this game will likely disappoint.

Black Sand Drift is a side-scroller shoot'em with partial controller support. Otherwise you are on the keyboard in your fight for freedom for the union of planets.
The game has a slightly 80s edge to it, with bold colours, boxy art and an interesting soundtrack that at times feels a bit out of place and melancholy. It's not one I would expect in a space shoot-em up type game. The tutorial is well detailed, easy to get to grips with and even extols the virtues of the cheat option within the game.
Each “planet” consists of about 5 levels, boasting 25 in total. The game as an unique soundtrack for each level, and there are some pretty trippy “filters” you can use for the game – changing graphics so they're pastel, inverted, and eye-bleeding. Saturation and Hue can be fiddled around as well, but they're really just fluff controls and don't do anything towards the atmosphere of the game.
Black Sand Drift is a difficult game to score. On one hand it has its own charm and will appeal to enthusiasts of Space Invaders, and Galaga, but it can become quite tedious on the sense s and if you can't get past the rustic, rough graphics and art style, you may be best spending your money elsewhere. BSD offers a prominent story through the game which sets it apart from standard shoot-em ups but whether this is enough to encourage a complete play through really depends on if you feel the game is nostalgic or frustrating.
Good in a bundle or sale.

An archetype of good game design from start through finish. Such an interesting world that it not only makes you want to explore and uncover every detail the different areas have to offer, but makes newcomers to the material like myself want to read the graphic novels and discover more of the backstories and universe.
The strength of Batman: Arkham Asylum is not its source material, which is fantastic and rich, nor its visuals and art style, which match and bolster the content excellently, nor is it any single facet of the game. Instead, Arkham Asylum is an awesome experience because every aspect has been designed with gameplay in mind, and it delivers on every front.
*
perhaps stands out in it's fluidity and solidarity. Combat is deep, both practical and intelligent and works as well on keyboard as it does on controller.
* The upgrades and
systems deserve special mention. They're some of the most rich and interesting collectibles I've ever seen and make you want to explore every one of the multitude of components, and most of them actually add to the game. They also do their source material justice.
*
are also something special. It made me aware of how many plot driven games I've played where the voice acting and/or characters have been jarring, annoying, boring or simply immaterial. Nothing in this game is boring.
For the balance of review I tried to find something negative to say about Batman AA, and I just couldn't. I could mention that there're things which would've been nice additions, like certain larger, lifeless parts of the map having more moving/interacting parts or people, but that's purely me being a snob.
There's nothing in here which takes away from the game.
The GOTY content adds 3D mode which is fun, but nothing special, and some challenge maps, which are pretty fun, especially if you've exhausted all the content of the main game. As far as I know, all retailers now bundle the GOTY content at the same price, so it's a non factor.
Reviews and opinions on the following two in the series (Arkham City and Arkham Origins) vary, and each stand up fine on their own, but they're different in terms of approach and. in my opinion, less tight and perfected than Asylum.

Probably the best fighter ever made. I've now not only played through this 3 times (Normal and Hard while it was under GFWL and hard again with Steam) but also 100% it twice (GFWL and Steam).
Yes, City made the Freeflow Combat System better but it lost a lot of the intensity that this game had by going full-sandbox, so there are ways this game could be improved but not many. The flow system is brilliant: a smooth and constant combat system that requires more skill than luck with cinematic-like results that actually make you feel powerful. I wish this system or variants of it were used in many more games, I have yet to see a better way to do melee.
The mood, music, voices - all what you expect from Batman and Gotham. The world is dark and drab but not flat and completely lifeless. I don't want to say it looks pretty per se but it looks right. The only problem is you're probably going to spend 90% of the game in Dective Mode. It's just too handy to have things highlighted for you and is probably one of the few failings - unless you don't mind having a lot of stuff to collect at the end. Still, something like an augmented-reality where you only need full-detective mode for... detecting but still benefit from a sort of enhanced vision all the time would have been preferable.
The story isn't complex but it is engaging: something's fishy, things go wrong in a hurry, and you're stuck trying to rescue hostages and chase down Joker while having goons and super-villians thrown at you, trying to slow you down. Only weak spots, I felt, were Killer Croc's lair and Scarecrow's world - you'll probably feel what I mean if you play through it too. Croc's was just a bit out of place and Scarecrow wasn't bad, it just messed with the view and made combat a more tricky proposition.
The challenges aren't impossible but plan on getting frusterated by them, the last 2 combat ones were my personal bane but someone less devious could easily have issues with the predator (stealth) missions too.

There's a good mix of the puzzle and platformer elements in the climbing sections and its challenging enough, even on the regular level setting.  Whilst the game is quite "samey" in that involves exploring climbing and a bit of combat, its fulfilling eough

Although there are some flaws, the game is extremelly enjoyable, and as its price is very low now, it is a good catch.
Pros:
The designers created a truly horrific atmosphere: the game has scenes of sexual abuse, cannibalism and bleak morality, alhtough none of them are gratuitous
Good design: the game uses brutality to inform its simple mechanics.
You have to scale buildings, using windowsills and drainpipes for handholds, to achieve your objectives, and all those actions are tense because of your limited stamina - if your stamina reaches zero, you will fall to your death. So, the game forces you to use your resources at the right time or you will fail.
The game's setting – an American city, with all its skyscrapers cracked and its streets empty save for abandoned, rusting roadblocks.
Combat is tense too. Your char will always be short of ammunition, but will be facing large groups of enemies. Because of this setup, you will be forced to use surprise and your environment to survive. (as an example, in one of the encounter one of the best solutions is to slice the throat of the first person to get too close, then pull a gun on the remaining bandits and force them to back up against a ledge before kicking them to their deaths).
The bow and its two arrows (believe me, this one deserves the praise - you will be using it a lot)
Cons:
Because you face so many enemies from middle to the end of the game, you will end up repeating the same encounter many times, always following the same routine: surprise kill, shoot, ledge kick, etc.
The climbing, while tense, can become a grind, specially in the beginning of the game.
The ending: it seems the game was finished midway of its story. So, the main reason of the character going all the hardships will not be answered.
The combat system is innovative, though clearly not fully realized. The game is short enough to serve as a fun demonstration of twists on common mechanical tropes in 3rd person action games.

To summarize things: Mandagon is - in my opinion - a beautifully made game with a lot of thought and heart put into it.
ART - 9.5/10
I love, love, love pixel art, so I am probably biased, but I thought the art in this game was amazing. There is so much detail and I enjoyed every little bird, plant, the shrines, the big temple, the houses, the water, the snow ... should I go on? It has a very distinct Tibetan touch and it makes you feel like you got teleported into a little pixel Himalayan region. It's absolutely beautiful.
MUSIC - 8/10
The music sounded ominous and a little disharmonic and spooky, but kinda ... ethereal? I found it to be very fitting in regards to the place and the story.
STORY - 8/10
The more wisdom totems you speak to, the better you can figure out what's going on. I do not want to spoil anything for anyone, but there is symbolism around to help you understand too (the six big murals/pictures on the walls as you ascend in an elevator) and if you pay a little attention to any of the totems, the ending of the game will make you go 'ahh, I knew it was about xy'. It's not very hard to follow but nice to figure out imo. I enjoyed it and it fit the atmosphere and feeling of the game.
CONTROLS - 7/10
Some people are whining about how hard and unforgiving the jumps are, but I found them to be very forgiving and only messed up one jump in ~60 minutes of playing and found them to be pretty forgiving. Besides the 'tricky jumping', the controls were easy to adapt to.
Suggestions/bugs:
Controller optimaziton was a little messed up as both X and A made you jump, although X was supposed to be the action button, so it made taking elevators pretty much impossible as you would just jump instead of ride, over and over again. Additionally, if you weren't holding down on right or left while taking one of the glowing elevators, it would take you up and then down again, without letting you get off.
Definitely play with keyboard and mouse!
OVERALL - 8/10
It's pretty, it's relaxing, it's only about an hour long, and well, it's free! I found it well worth the time and was actually a bit sad it was so short. I will be buying the DLC because I enjoyed the game a lot and I'd love to see some more games by Blind Sky Studios.

I need to say that I'm definitely not in the right mindstate when I tried out this game, and had to abandon it since this game has little room for a preoccupied mind.
Even though I have some peeves, I have to admit that it's a well made, simple atmospheric genre game.
It would also be interesting to see this game being translated to different languages, predominantly to languages of regions where Buddhism is a common practice.
If your mind is often filled with darting thoughts, need for constant action and interaction, feeling aggressive and irritated, you won't like this game at all.

It's chill and Zen and whatnot, but... it reminds me too much of those side-scrollers on the Nintendo growing up. The ones I could never beat because I didn't have good enough hand-eye coordination.
I want to like it. I don't care for the music, but it seems like a game where you just kinda figure stuff out as you go along. And apparently the game is beatable in ~30 minutes. As I have put over an hour into this, I seem to be one of those folks who can't figure out "obvious" methods (probably by using Youtube or whatnot). But it also frustrates me. You can access the map at specific points, but after my last fall from a really high-up point where I missed one stupid jump onto a thin podium out of about 57, and then thought I could land on something but then saw I couldn't and tried to land on something else... and I basically fell from the top left of the map to the complete bottom. Into water. And I really had no idea how to find another map area, or get back to where I was.
Pros: Cool theme, chill ideas, I'd probably put more if I owned a Nintendo growing up and didn't rely on my 3 minutes of fail before I died and handed the controller to my friend who owned it til (s)he died... which was like 30+ minutes later.
Cons: The music clangs, and I really don't care enough to bother to understand what's going on here. I've found the game too frustrating with the lack of anything specified (I mean ffs, I'm a block of stone, why not just sit there?). Weird (and possibly disturbing) pictures of lungs. Cryptic messages that go over my head. And I'm not even blonde -- though I suspect that I just can't get into the game to care enough. Maybe it's because I don't do mind-altering/recreational/illegal substances?
Overall, hey it's free, the graphics are kinda cool (as is the map), the idea isn't half bad, and for a game beatable in under 30 minutes, it's already taken over an hour of my life. So I guess it's okay... but honestly, I wouldn't recommend it without a huge disclaimer: if you want to figure out a game that's chill with no real purpose aside from traipsing around Tibet with monks giving you cryptic rhymes... then do it!
That, and my recommendation would be based on the person I am talking to.
